+## Cost provenance
+
+Cost is not a single fact. `cost_status` separates how the number was obtained:
+
+| Status | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `reported` | The runtime stated a monetary total for its own execution |
+| `derived` | Citadel summed a breakdown the same runtime published |
+| `unavailable` | No trusted cost telemetry exists for this branch |
+
+Claude reports a total in `total_cost_usd`. When that field is absent, the CLI
+may still publish a per-model `costUSD` breakdown; its sum is recorded as
+`derived`, never as `reported`. A breakdown missing any entry's own cost would
+understate the charge, so the whole derivation fails closed to `unavailable`. A
+runtime-stated zero is a `reported` zero; missing telemetry never becomes one.
+
+Codex exec publishes token usage but no monetary field, so its cost is
+`unavailable`. Token counts are never priced into money: a per-token estimate
+would be Citadel's guess, not the runtime's evidence.
+
+Provenance travels in the stored cost `source` rather than a new field, so
+records written before this distinction keep their meaning. Each source is
+registered against exactly one runtime. A stored cost carrying a source no
+registered adapter emits, or one belonging to a different runtime than the
+branch that ran, is not evidence: the observation is rejected rather than
+displayed with the cost quietly removed.
+
